ARTEMIS II NASA's Artemis II SLS (Space Launch System) moon rocket with the Orion spacecraft slowly rolls back towards the Vehicle Assembly Building at the Kennedy Space Center, Wednesday, Feb. 25, 2026, in Cape Canaveral, Fla. (AP Photo/John Raoux) ARTEMIS II Where to watch the historic Artemis II launch on the Space Coast BY Spectrum News Staff Brevard County PUBLISHED 11:55 AM ET Mar. 31, 2026 PUBLISHED 11:55 AM EDT Mar. 31, 2026 SHARE BREVARD COUNTY, Fla. — On Wednesday evening, the four members of NASA's Artemis II mission will prepare for a flyby of the moon. It will be the first time in more than 50 years that humans have visited Earth’s sister. The two-hour launch window opens at 6:24 p.m. ET. Artemis II Coverage NASA to launch Artemis II crew in flyby mission to the moon Artemis II to bring traffic backups to Brevard County How to see Artemis II pass by the moon Artemis II highlights a series of firsts Meet the Artemis crew in NASA's first astronaut mission to the moon in more than a half-century MORE ON DESTINATION SPACE If you are planning to view the historic launch on the Space Coast, there are many easy-to-access sites to watch Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral rocket launches. Here are a few locations to start with: Marina Park Sand Point Park Playalinda Beach Space View Park Parrish Park View this map for more launch viewing location options: &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;nbsp; Watching from home? For others who would like to watch from their backyard, NASA has tracked where skywatchers in Florida and southern Georgia can view Artemis II's liftoff.
